identity.libraryClass: hand-rolled indexing (forecast[t+h] = y[t+h-s*ceil(h/s)]); statsforecast.models.SeasonalNaive is the library equivalent
identity.description: The family FLOOR: forecast every future period as the value from the same position in the last observed seasonal cycle. Zero parameters, zero fit. It exists to be beaten — MASE is defined against it, so it IS the denominator of the family's honest scoreboard.

consumes.note: regular time-indexed numeric series with at least one complete seasonal cycle of trailing history

emits.note: the last observed cycle tiled across the horizon; intervals only via an in-sample-residual wrapper, which is a generic calibration add-on, not the method — so 'none'

learnsVsFixed.note: the family's untrainable member: nothing is estimated — 'fit' merely stores the last observed cycle, and seasonal_periods is supplied configuration, not a learned quantity. Reusable as a fixed reference on any series with a known cadence.

seasonal_periods.note: a structural CONFIG set from the known cadence of the series, never searched — tuning the floor would move the goalpost the whole family is scored against

invariances.why: the forecast is a copy of observed values; rescaling the series rescales the copies identically
copying commutes with ANY pointwise transform: f(y[t-s]) is exactly the seasonal-naive forecast of the transformed series — the family's only transform-invariant member
a NaN anywhere in the last cycle is copied verbatim into the forecast — the mechanism propagates gaps rather than tolerating them
the series port contract is numeric; copying is dtype-agnostic in principle, but the family's port carries numeric-time-indexed values only
no likelihood, no stationarity, no error model — nothing is assumed because nothing is estimated
needs exactly one complete seasonal cycle — the smallest seasonal history requirement in the family; with less it cannot index y[t-s] at all
covers any horizon by tiling the last cycle — it never extrapolates a trend, which is precisely the blind spot trend-capable members exploit to beat it

featureStats.why: high seasonal strength is exactly when this floor is STRONG — candidates must beat it precisely where seasonality dominates, which is what makes MASE honest
trend is the floor's blind spot: last season's values are systematically off by one season of drift, quantifying how much headroom trend-capable models have
the existence gate — below 1 complete cycle the method is undefined and the floor degrades to last-value naive

modelMetrics.why: this model IS the MASE denominator — its own score is 1.0 by construction; it is in the catalog so every other family member has a fixed, untunable reference to beat on a time-ordered holdout

edgeCases.condition: history shorter than one full seasonal cycle
edgeCases.behavior: y[t-s] does not exist; method undefined

edgeCases.condition: NaN inside the last observed cycle
edgeCases.behavior: NaN copied directly into the forecast
systematically phase-misaligned forecast that looks plausible
edgeCases.note: cross-check the configured s against the ACF peak / seasonal_strength stat

edgeCases.behavior: perfect forecast — the floor is unbeatable and every candidate's MASE is undefined-ish (0/0 flavor)
edgeCases.note: flag the series as degenerate for the whole family, not just this member

driver.constructor: no fit — store the trailing s values; forecast[t+h] = stored_cycle[(h-1) mod s]
driver.wrapperNeeds: series adapter: (time_col, value_col, freq, horizon) + seasonal_periods config; 'fit' is a no-op that stores the last cycle buffer

placementClaims.why: gaps in the last cycle propagate verbatim into the forecast; time-aware fill must run first
copying commutes with any pointwise transform (monotoneTransformInvariant true) — transforming before or after yields the identical forecast
single numeric series has nothing to encode
